rounds.text: Alicon Castalloy is currently undergoing a significant transformation as its capital expenditure cycle concludes, evidenced by a 45.5% reduction in capital work-in-progress [E40]. This transition into a phase of operational capacity is supported by robust growth metrics, including a 29% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E17] and a 17% increase in profit growth over the same period [E21]. The company’s operational efficiency is improving, as seen in the reduction of working capital requirements from 24.8 days to 11.6 days [E61], while cash generation remains strong with a 7.03x cash conversion ratio [E34]. Institutional confidence is rising, reflected in a positive money flow and an increase in domestic institutional holdings from 9.00% to 11.29% [E43, E44]. Conceded: the company faces headwinds from a declining operating margin [E30, E31], a low return on equity [E13, E69], and a valuation that currently exceeds its discounted cash flow intrinsic value [E45, E46]. Despite these challenges, the stock maintains strong momentum, trading at its 52-week high with a relative strength rating of 100 [E48, E51].

Alicon Castalloy Ltd trades at an aggressive P/E of 43.2x to 43.73x, sitting significantly above its sector benchmark of 23.92x [E1, E6]. This rich valuation is hard to justify given weak capital efficiency: the company delivers a low ROE of 6.28% to 7.0% and an ROCE of 9.27% to 10.6%, both trailing sector benchmarks substantially [E8, E9, E10, E12, E13]. Profitability is further compromised by a three-year compounded profit growth of -6% and a contracting operating margin that dropped 3 percentage points down to 10% in the TTM period [E20, E30]. Moreover, borrowings have escalated to ₹ 412 Cr as of September 2026, rising from ₹ 354 Cr in the prior year [E39]. From a valuation standpoint, a discounted cash flow model puts intrinsic value at ₹ 993 per share against a market price of ₹ 1,076, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -8.3% [E45, E46]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing twelve-month sales growth of 29% alongside positive institutional money flows [E17, E44].

While the bear highlights a high P/E multiple [E1, E6], it ignores that Alicon Castalloy Ltd trades at an EV/EBITDA of 9.85x, which is actually below the sector benchmark of 11.83x [E11]. Conceded: the ROE and ROCE trail sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10, E12, E13], but the business is compounding top-line growth aggressively with a 29% sales surge in the trailing twelve months and a rules-based screen score of 84 out of 100 [E17, E64]. On the margin front, the bear points to declining operating margins [E30], yet overlooks that working capital requirements have drastically improved, dropping from 24.8 days to just 11.6 days [E61]. Regarding the increased borrowings of ₹ 412 Cr [E39], capital work-in-progress dropped by 45.5% to ₹ 42 Cr, signaling that major capital expenditures are completed and new revenue-generating capacity is coming online [E40]. Finally, while the bear cites a DCF intrinsic value of ₹ 993 [E45], profits are fully backed by cash with an exceptional cash conversion ratio of 7.03x yielding ₹ 239 Cr in operating cash flow and ₹ 93 Cr in free cash flow [E34, E35, E36], supported by a positive sector tailwind score of +1.10 [E73].

Conceded: EV/EBITDA is 9.85x against a sector benchmark of 11.83x [E11]. However, relying on this single metric ignores that the company’s P/E of 43.2x to 43.73x heavily outpaces the sector benchmark of 23.92x [E1, E6]. While the bull points to strong TTM sales growth of 29% [E17], 3-year compounded profit growth sits at -6% [E20] and operating margins have compressed by 3 percentage points to 10% [E30, E31]. The assertion that completed capital expenditures and lower working capital requirements [E40, E61] excuse the risk is undermined by borrowings rising to ₹ 412 Cr from ₹ 354 Cr [E39] alongside a low ROE of 7% [E13] and median ROE of just 9% over 3, 5, and 10 years [E26, E27, E28]. Furthermore, dismissing the DCF intrinsic value of ₹ 993 [E45] based on cash flow ignores that the current share price of ₹ 1,076 sits above that intrinsic value [E45], resulting in a negative margin of safety of -8.3% [E46].
